The paper introduces a novel IQA paradigm, its core novelty lies in integrating multimodal referring/grounding with image quality assessment, consisting of two subtasks (GIQA-DES and GIQA-VQA). It constructs the GIQA-160K dataset via an automated annotation pipeline and the GIQA-Bench benchmark, enabling more fine-grained image quality evaluation.

Key concerns—such as comparison with more advanced models, demonstration of the IQA method’s generalization, and introduction of a user study—were adequately addressed during the rebuttal. Overall, the work is easy to follow and the experiments are comprehensive. I recommend accepting this paper and think this work is a strong fit for the ***"Datasets and Benchmarks"*** track.
Thank you for flagging U2TN. This feedback has been taken into account in the decision.
